text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Long COVID can be considered a disability under the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if it substantially limits one or more major life activities. The definition of "major life activities" is broad, including things like caring for oneself, working, and concentrating.

list.title: ADA Definition:
list.snippet: The ADA defines a disability as a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities.

list.title: Long COVID and Major Life Activities:
list.snippet: Long COVID can affect various major life activities, such as:
Working: Difficulty concentrating, fatigue, and other symptoms can impact job performance.
Caring for oneself: Individuals may struggle with basic tasks like getting dressed or eating.
Other activities: Long COVID can also affect breathing, walking, thinking, and other essential functions.

list.title: Individualized Assessment:
list.snippet: Whether Long COVID qualifies as a disability under the ADA depends on the specific individual and the extent to which their symptoms limit their major life activities.

list.title: Legal Guidance:
list.snippet: The Department of Justice and the Department of Health and Human Services have issued guidance stating that Long COVID can be a disability under the ADA.

text_blocks.snippet: Long COVID, also known as long-haul COVID, refers to ongoing health problems that can persist for weeks, months, or even years after the initial COVID-19 infection. These long-term effects are triggered by the virus that causes COVID-19 and are not contagious. Anyone who has had a SARS-CoV-2 infection can experience Long COVID, even if they didn't have noticeable symptoms during the initial illness.
snippet_highlighted_words: ongoing health problems that can persist for weeks, months, or even years after the initial COVID-19 infection

text_blocks.snippet: Common symptoms of Long COVID include:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath: Difficulty breathing or feeling winded.
Cognitive dysfunction: Problems with memory, concentration, and thinking (also known as brain fog).
Sleep disturbances: Difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or experiencing restful sleep.
Heart problems: Fast or irregular heartbeat.
Digestive issues: Problems like diarrhea, constipation, or bloating.
Other potential illnesses: Long COVID can also trigger or worsen conditions like migraine, lung disease, autoimmune diseases, and chronic kidney disease, according to the Mayo Clinic.

text_blocks.snippet: Long COVID is considered a chronic condition. It's triggered by the virus that causes COVID-19 and can lead to a variety of ongoing symptoms and conditions. These symptoms can manifest weeks or months after the initial infection and can vary greatly in severity and duration.
